summary: FibrX builds a structural health and corrosion monitoring system that pairs fiber optic sensors with cloud software (a platform-as-a-service, per its site). The sensing method comes from Naval Surface Warfare Center, Port Hueneme Division, and JumpStart says the company operates under a partially exclusive U.S. Navy license. Federal awards list Henderson, Nevada.
thesis: FibrX is trying to turn a Navy-patented method for detecting corrosion under coatings into a monitoring product for defense, aerospace and energy. It holds two small Defense Department R&D awards. The case rests on whether three people can field hardware.
stage: USAspending shows two federal awards to FibrX Inc, both signed in June 2026: an Air Force purchase order for $105,392 (ended 24 September 2026) and a NAVSEA contract labelled SBIR Phase I with $136,573 obligated and $234,840 including options (to 21 June 2027). Chloe Capital announced an investment on 17 February 2026, no amount stated. EDGAR has no filer named FibrX Inc, so no Form D is on record.

questions: Is the Navy patent license signed and in force, does it cover US 11,474,046 B2, and what are the field of use, royalty and milestone terms?
Has a sensor system been installed on a real asset, and what data shows the fiber detects corrosion rather than only strain and temperature?
What is FibrX building under NAVSEA topic N254-P02, an open topic for modular mine warfare components, and how does that work relate to the corrosion monitoring product?
How much equity money has been raised in total and on what terms (IAI CATALYST, Techstars, Chloe Capital, others)?
risks: No customer, pilot or installed system is named on the company's site. Four years after its 2022 startup studio cohort, federal obligations on record total $241,965 across two awards.
The core method is a Navy patent (US 11,474,046 B2), not the company's own. The signed agreement and its terms are not public.
The work is spread wide for three people: hypersonic and space systems (Air Force), naval mine components (NAVSEA topic), and bridges, oil and gas and offshore wind (site marketing).
unverified: A signed Navy patent license rests on the company's site and the JumpStart article, not independently confirmed.
What FibrX received from IAI, Techstars or Chloe Capital is not stated in any source. No amount could be confirmed.
The date and state of incorporation of FibrX Inc, and how it relates to the FibrX LLC in the Navy's 2022 story, are unconfirmed.
